Luonnonolot Filippiinit kuuluu niin sanottuun Tyynenmeren tulirengas -alueeseen, joka on altis luonnonkatastrofeille, kuten maanjäristyksille, tulivuorenpurkauksille ja pyörremyrskyille. Merenalaiset maanjäristykset voivat aiheuttaa myös hyökyaaltoja. Filippiineillä sijaitsee 22 aktiiviseksi luokiteltua tulivuorta. Filippiinejä koettelevat vuosittain useat pyörremyrskyt, joista pyritään varoittamaan etukäteen tiedotusvälineissä. Varsinainen sadekausi on kesäkuusta marraskuuhun, mutta pyörremyrskyjä voi esiintyä myös sadekauden ulkopuolella. Hirmumyrskyjen yhteydessä kannattaa ottaa huomioon myös tulva- ja maanvyörymävaarat, jotka voivat aiheuttaa suuriakin tuhoja. Hirmumyrskyn iskiessä, seurauksena voi olla välittömiä vaikutuksia infrastruktuuriin, sähkönjakeluun ja verkkoyhteyksiin. Elintarvikkeista, vedestä ja käteisvaluutasta voi olla puutetta. Erilaisiin luonnonmullistuksiin kannattaa varautua mahdollisuuksien mukaan etukäteen. Niiden aikana liikkuminen käy hankalaksi, jopa vaaralliseksi, ja paikoittain kulku- ja puhelinyhteydet voivat katketa kokonaan. Varoitukset ja viranomaisohjeet voivat tulla lyhyellä ennakointiajalla, joten paikallistiedotteita tulee seurata erityisen tarkkaavaisesti. Kun saapuu maahan ja poistuu maasta on täytettävä eTravel Pass jossa kysytään myös rokotuksista. Kesäkuusta marraskuuhun kestävällä sadekaudella Filippiinien terveysviranomaiset ovat antaneet varoituksia kulkutautien kasvavasta riskistä. Huolellisella hygienialla riskejä voi kuitenkin pienentää merkittävästi. Kuuma ja kostea ilmasto voi aiheuttaa rasitusta joillekin matkailijoille. Ainoa keino ehkäistä hyttysvälitteisen taudin tarttumista on suojautua hyttysten pistoilta käyttämällä karkotteita sekä pukeutumalla pitkähihaisiin ja -lahkeisiin vaaleisiin vaatteisiin. Muut turvallisuustason tiedot

Terrori-iskut ovat mahdollisia etenkin Etelä-Filippiinien Mindanaolla ja Metro-Manilassa. Seuraa säätietoja sadekaudella. Vältä kaikkea matkustamista Mindanaon lounaisosiin, Zamboangan niemimaalle ja Sulun saaristoon.

Ajankohtaista

Ajankohtaista tietoa Filippiinien tilanteesta löydät edustuston verkkosivuilta ja seuraamalla paikallisviranomaisten tiedotusta. Edustusto päivittää ajankohtaista tietoa myös sosiaalisen median kanavilleen.

UM:n matkustustiedotteet ovat suosituksia

Vastaat matkapäätöksestäsi aina itse. Paikallisilla viranomaisilla on ensisijainen vastuu kaikkien maan alueella oleskelevien ihmisten turvallisuudesta ja hätätilanteissa etsintä- ja pelastustoimista. Kriisitilanteissa noudata paikallisten viranomaisten ohjeita. Seuraa uutisointia tiedotusvälineissä sekä tiedotusta edustuston verkkosivuilla ja sosiaalisen median kanavissa. Ulkoministeriö ja Suomen ulkomaanedustustot avustavat suomalaisia konsulipalvelulain mukaisesti. Mikäli Euroopan unionin ulkopuolisessa kohdemaassa ei ole Suomen edustustoa, voit kääntyä muiden EU-maiden edustustojen puoleen. Matkatoimiston järjestämällä matkalla olevaa avustaa ensisijaisesti matkanjärjestäjä.

Konsulipalvelulaki
Konsulisuojeludirektiivi
Laki matkapalveluyhdistelmistä

Suosittelemme aina matkavakuutuksen ottamista. Tarkista ennen matkaasi matkavakuutuksesi kattavuus ja voimassaolo erityisesti jos sinulla on jokin sairaus, olet raskaana, matkasi suuntautuu vaarallisille alueille tai harrastat riskialttiita lajeja, Sairastuneen tai vainajan kotiuttaminen on kallista ja vaikea järjestää ilman kattavaa matkavakuutusta, eikä hoitoa aina saa ulkomailla ilman maksusitoumusta tai ennakkomaksua.

Tee matkustusilmoitus osoitteessa https://matkustusilmoitus.fi/

Yleinen turvallisuustilanne

Ulkoministeriö suosittelee noudattamaan erityistä varovaisuutta ja tarkkaavaisuutta julkisilla paikoilla liikuttaessa. Terrori-iskut ja/tai poliittiset levottomuudet eivät ole poissuljettuja.

Sisäpoliittinen tilanne on pääosin rauhallinen, mutta poliittiset mielenosoitukset ja väkijoukkojen kokoontumiset ovat mahdollisia. Rauhallisetkin mielenosoitukset voivat kasvaa kooltaan valtaviksi ja muuttua väkivaltaisiksi, väkijoukkojen kokoontumisia ei kannata mennä seuraamaan läheltä.

Paikallisten juhlapäivien aikaan valmiustilaa nostetaan entisestään. Julkiset tilat kuten linja-autoterminaalit, lauttasatamat, ostoskeskukset ja kirkot saattavat olla iskujen kohteina.

Turvallisuusjärjestelyt saattavat olla puutteellisia Manilan isoissa ostoskeskuksissa ja suuria väkijoukkoja houkuttelevissa tilaisuuksissa kuten konserteissa ja uskonnollisissa tapahtumissa.

Filippiinien viranomaiset muistuttavat säännöllisesti terrori-iskujen mahdollisuudesta. Terrori-iskujen ja muiden levottomuuksien mahdollisuus keskittyy Mindanaolle ja Sulun saaristoon, mutta myös pääkaupunkiseutu Metro-Manila ja muut merkittävät kaupungit voivat olla mahdollisia iskukohteita.

Keski-Visayasin saaristossa sekä Palawanin alueella, mukaan lukien Puerto Princesa City ja Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park, on olemassa pieni kidnappausriski ja terroriuhka.

Aseellisia välikohtauksia esiintyy Filippiinien armeijan ja muslimiseparatistien välillä Mindanaolla sekä kommunistisen ääriliikkeen alueilla muun muassa Pohjois-Luzonilla ja Itä-Mindanaolla.

Koko Mindanaon saarella on ollut voimassa poikkeustilalaki (martial law) terrorisminvastaisten operaatioiden vuoksi. Vaikka poikkeustilalaki päättyi vuoden 2019 lopussa, ei Mindanaon saarella ole päästy täysin normaalioloihin.

Mindanaolle matkustavien on syytä seurata tilannetta erityisen tarkasti paikallisista tiedotusvälineistä ja noudattaa paikallisviranomaisten määräyksiä.

Siviiliuhreja vaatineita yhteenottoja on tapahtunut myös Visayasin saaristossa Boholilla, osassa Keski-Mindanaota esimerkiksi Pohjois-Cotabaton, Lanao del Surin ja Lanao del Norten maakunnissa.

Pienimuotoisia pommi- ja kranaatti-iskuja on tapahtunut Mindanaon muslimialueiden (BARMM Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao) lisäksi muun muassa Cotabaton, Kidapawan, Zamboangan, General Santosin, Davaon, Illiganin ja Cagayan de Oron alueilla.

Terroristijärjestö Abu Sayyafin ja armeijan väliset yhteenotot jatkuvat Mindanaolla ja erityisesti Sulun saaristossa, mukaan lukien Basilanin, Tawi Tawin ja Jolon saarilla. Samoilla alueilla on viime vuosien aikana tapahtunut myös joitakin länsimaalaisten kidnappaustapatuksia.

Levottomuuksien, aseellisten yhteenottojen mahdollisuuden ja sieppausuhan vuoksi tulisi välttää matkustamista Mindanaon lounaisosiin, Zamboangan niemimaalle ja Sulun saaristoon.

Matkailua eristyksissä oleviin Etelä-Filippiinien rantakohteisiin ei suositella läheisillä merialueilla operoivien sieppausryhmien vuoksi. Sieppausten kohteena ovat useimmiten hallituksen edustajat tai varakkaat paikalliset, mutta matkailijan kannattaa silti noudattaa varovaisuutta.

Yleinen hätänumero on 911.

Rikollisuus

Köyhyydestä johtuva katurikollisuus on Filippiineillä yleistä. Muun muassa käsilaukkujen ryöstöt ovat tavanomaisia ja ne ovat johtaneet jopa henkirikoksiin. Ryöstäjät käyttävät usein moottoripyörää. Aika ajoin varoitetaan ostoskeskuksissa ja yökerhoissa yksin liikkuvia ryöstöistä, joissa voidaan käyttää lamaannuttavia kemikaaleja.

Pimeitä teitä ja väentungoksia kannattaa välttää, samoin kuin yksin matkustamista Metro-Manilan ulkopuolella ja öiseen aikaan myös kaupunkialueella. Taksikuskien tiedetään osallistuneen ryöstöihin. Taksi on suositeltavaa ottaa valvotulta alueelta kuten ostoskeskusten ja hotellien virallisilta taksitolpilta, jolloin taksin rekisterinumero kirjataan ylös. Nettitilauksena paikalle saatava Grab on suosittu, sillä matkan hinta määräytyy jo tilattaessa.

Vieraiden tarjoamiin juomiin ja ruokiin on syytä suhtautua varauksellisesti. Niihin on voitu lisätä tyrmäystippoja ryöstö- tai päällekarkausaikomuksissa.

Poliisin ja rikollisten välisten yhteenottojen ja ammuskelujen harhaluodit voivat vaatia myös ulkopuolisia uhreja. Näissä tilanteissa kannattaa poistua paikalta mahdollisimman nopeasti.

Huumausainerikoksiin suhtaudutaan erittäin ankarasti.

Henkilöllisyys on pystyttävä pyydettäessä todistamaan poliisille; tähän riittää yleensä passikopio.

Jos passisi katoaa tai varastetaan, tee siitä ilmoitus paikalliselle poliisiasemalle. Mikäli kohdemaassa ei ole Suomen edustustoa, hae hätämatkustusasiakirjaa (ETD = Emergency Travel Document) toisen EU-maan edustustosta.

Ota kopiot tärkeimmistä asiapapereista kuten passista ja lentolipuista. Säilytä ne erillään alkuperäisistä.

Liikenne

Liikennekulttuuri poikkeaa huomattavasti suomalaisesta. Kulkuvälineet voivat olla heikkokuntoisia, ja ajotyyli on ajoittain aggressiivista ja ennakoimatonta. Teiden kunto voi olla kaupungeissa ja erityisesti maaseudulla heikkoa. Yleensä filippiiniläisissä autoissa ei ole vakuutuksia, mikä on onnettomuuden sattuessa hyvä tietää.

Maan linja-autokanta on osittain heikkoa ja vanhaa. Kuolemiin johtaneita turmia tapahtuu pitkillä ajomatkoilla aika ajoin. Kehotamme noudattamaan harkintaa linja-autoyhtiön valinnassa. Yöaikaan kulkevat linjat eivät ole suositeltavia.

Etenkin Metro-Manilassa liikenneruuhkat voivat viivästyttää matkantekoa merkittävästi.

Armeijan ja poliisin tehostetut turvatarkastukset Metro-Manilan alueella sekä keskeisiksi luokitelluissa kohteissa, kuten lentokentillä, satamissa ja pääliikenneväylillä aiheuttavat viivästymisiä. Matkailijan kannattaa varautua autojen ja käsilaukkujen tarkastuksiin saavuttaessa julkisiin tiloihin, kuten ostoskeskuksiin ja hotelleihin.

Liikuntaesteisille Filippiinit on haasteellinen. Jalkakäytävät puuttuvat usein kokonaan, eikä omaehtoinen liikkuminen ole mahdollista. Kuljettajan ja henkilökohtaisen avustajan palkkaaminen on suhteellisen helppoa.

Laivaonnettomuuksia tapahtuu ajoittain, koska alukset ovat huonokuntoisia ja usein ylikuormitettuja, eikä turvamääräyksiä noudateta.

Luonnonolot

Filippiinit kuuluu niin sanottuun Tyynenmeren tulirengas -alueeseen, joka on altis luonnonkatastrofeille, kuten maanjäristyksille, tulivuorenpurkauksille ja pyörremyrskyille. Merenalaiset maanjäristykset voivat aiheuttaa myös hyökyaaltoja. Filippiineillä sijaitsee 22 aktiiviseksi luokiteltua tulivuorta.

Filippiinejä koettelevat vuosittain useat pyörremyrskyt, joista pyritään varoittamaan etukäteen tiedotusvälineissä. Varsinainen sadekausi on kesäkuusta marraskuuhun, mutta pyörremyrskyjä voi esiintyä myös sadekauden ulkopuolella. Hirmumyrskyjen yhteydessä kannattaa ottaa huomioon myös tulva- ja maanvyörymävaarat, jotka voivat aiheuttaa suuriakin tuhoja. Hirmumyrskyn iskiessä, seurauksena voi olla välittömiä vaikutuksia infrastruktuuriin, sähkönjakeluun ja verkkoyhteyksiin. Elintarvikkeista, vedestä ja käteisvaluutasta voi olla puutetta.

Erilaisiin luonnonmullistuksiin kannattaa varautua mahdollisuuksien mukaan etukäteen. Niiden aikana liikkuminen käy hankalaksi, jopa vaaralliseksi, ja paikoittain kulku- ja puhelinyhteydet voivat katketa kokonaan. Varoitukset ja viranomaisohjeet voivat tulla lyhyellä ennakointiajalla, joten paikallistiedotteita tulee seurata erityisen tarkkaavaisesti.

Lisätietoja:

  • Filippiinien meteorologian laitos, PAGASA (englanniksi)
  • Filippiinien vulkanologian ja seismologian laitos, PHIVOLCS (englanniksi)
  • Filippiinien katastrofikeskus, NDRRMC (englanniksi)
  • Ohjeita maanjäristystilanteeseen, Helsingin yliopiston seismologian laitos
  • Tyynenmeren tsunamikeskus, PTWC (englanniksi)
  • Kansainvälinen tsunamikeskus International Tsunami Information Center (englanniksi)
  • Maailmanlaajuinen maanjäristystietokanta, USGS (englanniksi)
Terveys

Kaiken kattava matkustajavakuutus on tarpeen. Kun saapuu maahan ja poistuu maasta on täytettävä eTravel Pass jossa kysytään myös rokotuksista.

Kesäkuusta marraskuuhun kestävällä sadekaudella Filippiinien terveysviranomaiset ovat antaneet varoituksia kulkutautien kasvavasta riskistä. Huolellisella hygienialla riskejä voi kuitenkin pienentää merkittävästi. Kuuma ja kostea ilmasto voi aiheuttaa rasitusta joillekin matkailijoille.

Vesijohtoveden laadun vuoksi on turvallisinta juoda pullotettua vettä.

Filippiineillä esiintyy hyttysten levittämää dengue- ja chikungunyakuumetta sekä zikavirusta. Myös malariaa esiintyy alueittain. Ainoa keino ehkäistä hyttysvälitteisen taudin tarttumista on suojautua hyttysten pistoilta käyttämällä karkotteita sekä pukeutumalla pitkähihaisiin ja -lahkeisiin vaaleisiin vaatteisiin. Erityisen tärkeää suojautuminen on raskaana oleville. Myös rabiesta eli vesikauhua esiintyy eri puolilla Filippiinejä. Kontaktia eläimiin, erityisesti koiriin ja kissoihin, kannattaa välttää.

Filippiinien terveysministeriö (englanniksi)

Selvitä ennakkoon matkakohteesi tartuntatautitilanne ja rokotussuositukset. Löydät ne seuraavien viranomaisten verkkosivuilta:
Matkailijan terveysopas
Maailman terveysjärjestö WHO
Euroopan tartuntatautivirasto

Maan lait ja käytännöt

Matkailija on velvollinen noudattamaan paikallista lainsäädäntöä. Tuomiokäytäntö esimerkiksi huumausainerikoksissa on eurooppalaisittain ajatellen ankara. Myös pienen huumemäärän hallussapidosta voidaan tuomita vankeutta. Lasten seksuaalinen hyväksikäyttö on Filippiineillä rangaistava teko, jonka tuomiona on yleensä vankeutta.

Maahantulosäännökset

Matkustusrajoitukset voivat muuttua nopeasti, joten on tärkeää seurata ajantasaisia viranomaistiedotteita, suurlähetystön verkkosivuja ja sosiaalista mediaa.

title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
summary: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes. But what happens when the rest of the internet won’t play nice? In recent weeks, users of services like Meta’s Muse, xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Yelp told TechCrunch that it only allows AI agents that pay for its data licensing program, while Delta Air Lines is preventing them from booking tickets on behalf of users. JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab have also confirmed that they’re blocking AI agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns. Some users say sites that previously worked with their AI agent are no longer accessible, including Cars.com and Amtrak, suggesting other companies could be quietly blocking them.
summary_html:
Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes. But what happens when the rest of the internet won’t play nice?

In recent weeks, users of services like Meta’s Muse, xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Yelp told TechCrunch that it only allows AI agents that pay for its data licensing program, while Delta Air Lines is preventing them from booking tickets on behalf of users. JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab have also confirmed that they’re blocking AI agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns. Some users say sites that previously worked with their AI agent are no longer accessible, including Cars.com and Amtrak, suggesting other companies could be quietly blocking them.

title: Krybit Ransomware: What You Need to Know
summary: Krybit is the name of a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation that first surfaced in early 2026. The group rents out the ransomware it has developed to affiliates who carry out attacks on its behalf, splitting ransoms extorted from victims 80:20 (80% to affiliates, 20% to the Krybit operators) in exchange for access to the malware, a dashboard, and round-the-clock technical support. As with most other modern ransomware operations, Krybit steals data before encrypting the original copies, threatening to publish the information it has exfiltrated on its leak site if the victim does not give in to the extortionists' demands.

title: Vulnerability in NordVPN software
summary: Classification: Important, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 6.8, CVEs: CVE-2026-106030, Summary: The vulnerability CVE-2026-106030: NordVPN for Windows allows local attackers to stop unprotected Windows system services and change their startup type to Manual via named pipes. The NordVPN user-mode application allows a low-privileged attacker to act as a trusted process and connect to the named pipe \\.\pipe\nord-security\v1\NordVpnService\Server. The attacker can then invoke the ISettingsGrpc.StopService and ISettingsGrpc.ChangeServiceStartType methods with an arbitrary service name, allowing them to stop any unprotected Windows service and change its startup type. This leads to denial of service of critical system services. Services protected by Windows (PPL processes, Windows Tamper Protection), such as Windows Defender, cannot be stopped or reconfigured.

title: Irish police force has its Twitter hacked in cryptocurrency scam
summary: There must have been red faces in the social media department of Ireland's police headquarters after two of its accounts were hijacked this week. The official @GardaInfo and @GardaTraffic Twitter accounts of Garda Síochána were accessed by an unauthorised third party who posted cryptocurrency-related messages on Wednesday evening, potentially reaching hundreds of thousands of users. The messages claimed that followers were eligible to claim free cryptocurrency through an airdrop. However, victims who followed the link could potentially be tricked into handing over the keys to their cryptocurrency wallet, and end up with their savings drained. The problem, however, is not just that a hacker found themselves with the ability to post fraudulent messages posing as the Irish police. If an unauthorised person was able to publish unauthorised posts from the accounts they may also have been able to access direct messages (DMs) which could contain sensitive personal information from members of the public.

title: ConnectWise Suspends Cloud Backup After Attackers Compromise Microsoft 365 Tenants
summary: ConnectWise on Saturday said it has disabled seven ConnectWise application identities as it continues its investigation into an incident in which unknown threat actors obtained unauthorized access to the application identities and compromised Microsoft 365 tenants. The IT management software provider said it took the action on October 17, 2026, at 07:00 UTC, adding it has also suspended Cloud Backup service by revoking certificates used for affected application connections across all users. "Disabling the affected connections prevents new authentication through those connections; it does not reverse changes previously made inside a tenant," it said. "The affected shared Cloud Backup credentials are no longer valid. Previously issued access tokens may remain usable until they expire or are otherwise invalidated. Any unauthorized credentials, permissions, or other access established through separate identities require additional review and remediation."

title: Hackers exploit SiteGuard WAF flaw to run commands as admins
summary: Hackers are exploiting an OS command-injection vulnerability in the SiteGuard Server Edition web application firewall (WAF), allowing them to execute commands with root or SYSTEM privileges on affected machines. The security issue is tracked as CVE-2026-106931 and affects the statistics feature in host-based WAF instances, which is enabled by default. SiteGuard is a leading Japanese WAF vendor that claims to protect more than 1.5 million websites. Based on WordPress.org statistics, the product is active on 500,000 sites. According to the vendor’s bulletin and a warning from Japan's CERT agency, CVE-2026-106931 has critical severity and is currently being exploited in the wild. “An OS command injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-106931) has been found in the statistics function of SiteGuard Server Edition. Abuse has already been confirmed,” reads SiteGuard’s alert. The attacker’s identity, the victims, the scale of the attacks, and the methods used remain unclear, as neither security advisory provides these details.

title: CVE-2026-88771: Inside the Exploitation of a Critical NetScaler RCE Vulnerability
summary: On September 27, 2026, Citrix disclosed CVE-2026-88771, a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability affecting NetScaler Application Delivery Controller (ADC) and NetScaler Gateway. The vulnerability carries a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8 according to NVD and a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.5 according to the Citrix security bulletin CTX697096. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands on affected appliances. Exploitation requires no optional features to be enabled. Citrix confirmed exploitation on unmitigated appliances, and the US’s Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-88771 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of active exploitation worldwide. Citrix has since disclosed another critical vulnerability affecting NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway, CVE-2026-107406, which can lead to RCE or denial of service. CVE-2026-107406 affects appliances configured as SAML service provider or identity provider depending on the software version. The analysis in this blog focuses on the exploitation of CVE-2026-88771.

title: Cybercrims go beyond stealing data to attack physical building systems
summary: Late Sunday night, a still-unknown cybercriminal or group hacked thousands of remote-controlled refrigeration systems across hundreds of French grocery stores, spiking temperatures, spoiling food, and sparking fires. This is part of an ongoing trend of attacking physical systems that can do damage in the real world. In August, a ransomware attack disrupted building-management systems at a Canadian hospital, affecting door access controls, central HVAC monitoring, and the issuing of staff access cards. And three years ago, cyberattacks hit Las Vegas casinos, causing slot machines to go dark, preventing payment kiosks and ATMs from spitting out cash, and locking guests out of their rooms when the electronic keys stopped working. Not all digital intrusions remain in cyberspace, and attackers don’t need to encrypt files and steal data to cause chaos. Hitting physical systems often produces more severe consequences - and turns up the heat on executives to pay an extortion demand.

title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
summary: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own. The incident—which likely would have resulted in criminal charges had they been performed directly by a person—has further heightened concerns that widespread AI use could have harmful effects on an unprecedented scale.

title: MALFEX npm Package 'imgdecode' Hides Shellcode Loader in Windows Native Addon
summary: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a malicious npm package that's part of a recently disclosed software supply chain attack campaign dubbed MALFEX. The package, named "imgdecode," was uploaded to the package registry on September 30, 2026, by a user named "malfexteste8." It has been downloaded 979 times as of writing and is still available on npm as of writing. The latest version of the package is 1.0.3. "The npm package imgdecode hides a malicious loader in a compiled Node.js addon," SafeDep said. "Its nine-line JavaScript file loads a Windows dynamic-link library (DLL). When a Node.js program calls require('imgdecode') from a Windows console, the DLL attempts to download encrypted shellcode from GitHub. It decrypts the response and injects the result into a new dllhost.exe process."

title: Hackers breach Microsoft 365 tenants via ConnectWise supply-chain attack
summary: ConnectWise has shut down customer access to its Cloud Backup service (formerly SkyKick Cloud Backup) after hackers accessed application identities and compromised Microsoft 365 tenants. Reports of the malicious activity began emerging on Friday, with administrators observing unauthorized access to client data in Microsoft 365 tenants due to a potential “SkyKick/CW breach.” Later on the same day, managed cybersecurity and threat detection platform Huntress confirmed the worries, saying that it had identified at least 162 compromised tenants in its environment. In a post today, Microsoft also confirmed malicious activity involving ConnectWise’s Cloud Backup service, saying it identified unauthorized authentication attempts from an IP address on October 15. ConnectWise’s cloud backup solutions provide backup and recovery services that help managed service providers (MSPs) and IT teams protect and restore customer data, such as emails and files, in cloud environments including Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.

title: skynox7: Proxyjacking Edge Devices Into Residential Proxies
summary: Adversaries have a wide range of mechanisms they can use to obfuscate their public internet protocol (IP) addresses to avoid attribution and reduce their detectable signature. Adversaries have used various types of nodes and services to proxy their traffic including commercial virtual private networks (VPN), virtual private servers (VPS), co-opted victim infrastructure, and more. Over time, defenders have been able to use adversary choices in infrastructure to surface illegitimate activity. For example, “It’s not normal for our users to login from IP addresses associated with this or any VPS provider.” Some stealthy adversaries are using residential proxies, which fundamentally break some of the core assumptions about the detectable characteristics of infrastructure used for malicious activity. GreyNoise helped an organization identify one of these stealthy intrusions and separately revealed a malicious cyber actor conducting a proxyjacking campaign.

title: TAG-217 Targets South Korean Financial Services with ARTEX
summary: The threat actor linked to recent AI-assisted attacks on South Korean financial institutions was testing infrastructure and assembling attack tools as early as August 2026, weeks before the banking campaign became public, according to new research from Recorded Future’s Insikt Group. Subsequent public reporting indicated that the breaches exposed personal data belonging to at least 68,000 people across at least seven financial institutions. Insikt Group’s investigation expands the known timeline and capabilities of the actor, tracked as TAG-217. Insikt Group uncovered tools designed to steal cryptocurrency wallet files, gain greater access to Linux systems, and test weaknesses in mobile devices. The findings illustrate the “jagged edge” of AI-enabled attacks: threat actors realizing significant gains while committing basic operational security mistakes. AI helps attackers pursue more targets across more environments, but does not prevent them from making the security mistakes that allowed Recorded Future to uncover preparations and capabilities beyond the reported banking campaign. Those mistakes give defenders opportunities to identify related activity and disrupt operations.

title: Moxa Vulnerabilities in Industrial Computing Products
summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 8.6, CVEs: CVE-2026-109812, CVE-2026-109813, Summary: This security advisory addresses two vulnerabilities identified in industrial computing products. CVE-2026-109812 - Missing Authorization on Secret Endpoints A missing authorization vulnerability exists in the internal API `/api/v1/secrets/` of some of Moxa's industrial computing products. A low-privileged authenticated attacker with adjacent network access could exploit this vulnerability to access sensitive information, potentially resulting in the disclosure of confidential data, including cryptographic key material. CVE-2026-109813 - Shared Hard-coded Root CA Private Key A hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability exists in the `/usr/bin/sysman` of some of Moxa's industrial computing products. An unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access could exploit the exposed private key material to compromise the confidentiality and integrity of communications.

title: Investigating Ephemeral Supply Chain Tampering
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant investigated a software supply chain compromise campaign targeting the update infrastructure belonging to AOMEI Technology between April 2026 and July 2026. The threat actor conducted repeated, short-burst configuration tampering against AOMEI origin servers. Each tampering window remained active for only five to ten minutes before reverting to authentic versions. This is the first time that we have encountered a software supply chain compromise that was implemented with these very short windows, effectively evading traditional point-in-time triage and automated file scanning. The campaign delivered a multi-stage payload chain involving the newly tracked CROSSROAD downloader and SHINYROAD backdoor. The threat actor iteratively modified its tradecraft, pivoting its staging infrastructure from cloud providers to dedicated domains and legitimate cloud storage. This evolving staging setup makes it particularly challenging for defenders to establish effective infrastructure-based blocking or network controls. We attribute this activity to a threat cluster we are tracking as UNC7017.

title: AI-Powered Espionage Campaign Targets Government Linux Infrastructure
summary: Unit 42 identified a campaign targeting government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure, with observed activity spanning from October 2025–April 2026. We track this activity as CL-UNK-1211. In the operations we witnessed, the attackers relied on AI-generated payloads. Multiple artifacts deployed throughout the intrusion contained AI-made conversational annotations and developer reasoning comments, suggesting that the code was either generated using large language models (LLMs) or executed by an automated AI agent. The attackers behind this cluster of activity focused on Linux environments to conduct extensive reconnaissance and maintain persistent network access to support intelligence-gathering. The attackers attempted to dump sensitive databases and exfiltrate government mailboxes to access social media accounts. The campaign included a diverse toolkit that combined open-source tools, custom cross-platform backdoors and widespread web shell deployments. We observed various defense evasion techniques, including attempts to disable endpoint protections, erase system logs and plant deceptive red-team markers to disguise activity as a legitimate security assessment. Our attribution of this activity to CL-UNK-1211 is in accordance with the Unit 42 attribution framework. We designate the term UNK to clusters of activity whose affiliation with either nation-state or cybercrime activity we have not yet determined.

title: BAE Systems cyberattack disrupts US federal court operations
summary: The Administrative Office of the US Courts (AOUSC) says a cyberattack on government contractor BAE Systems has taken down the notice system used by federal bankruptcy courts. In a Thursday press release, the Administrative Office of the US Courts said the BAE Systems cyberattack also halted the production and distribution of bankruptcy notices. "The Administrative Office of the US Courts has been in communication with the impacted courts and is also coordinating with BAE Systems. BAE is actively investigating this incident and working to restore operations," AOUSC said. "As a result of the incident, all access to the BNC systems and websites that BAE operates on behalf of the Judiciary and the related bankruptcy noticing process are unavailable at this time, including bnc.uscourts.gov, bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov, notices.uscourts.gov, and the National Creditor Registration Service."

title: F-Secure Launches Victim-First Scam Encyclopedia Covering 50+ Types of Consumer Fraud
summary: There are more than 50 distinct ways to scam someone online, and F-Secure's Threat Intelligence team catalogued them all in its new Scam Encyclopedia,one of the most comprehensive guides to scams and fraudavailable today. Built from decades of research, the continuously updated, living guide covers both established scams and new methods most people haven't heard of yet. Unlike similar resources available online, the Scam Encyclopedia emphasizes a different point of view: every scam is explained from the victim's perspective, covering what they see, what they're told, what they're asked to do, and where exactly the "scam" comes in. That structure makes it easier for readers to recognize the same pattern in their own lives, before they become a victim themselves.

title: Exposing AdFection: How Discover-Tech Turned Targeted Ads Into a Pipeline for Zero-Click Mercenary Spyware
summary: This is the first-ever public confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered via targeted ads. We call the technique AdFection, and show how it was used to infect devices at Al Jazeera with Candiru’s spyware. We also uncover Discover-Tech, and show how the company helps mercenary surveillance vendors track and hack devices around the world. Devices at international news network Al Jazeera were infected with mercenary spyware from Candiru (rebranded as “Integrity Labs”) via targeted online advertisements. We provide the first public technical confirmation of a zero-click mercenary spyware attack delivered via targeted advertising, which we call AdFection. The malicious advertisements were purchased by Discover-Tech, an Israeli company that presents itself as a legitimate advertising company, but which we found operates as a facilitator for multiple mercenary spyware partners. Discover-Tech operates a platform called Controlium that enables its mercenary partners to de-anonymize, fingerprint, and automatically infect devices the moment an advertisement is rendered — a form of zero-click attack. Analysis of four billion Discover-Tech bidding records shows that during a four-month period, the company’s ads were shown on almost 200,000 unique websites and Android/iOS apps in dozens of countries.

title: BeyondTrust patches zero-day exploited in attacks since August
summary: BeyondTrust warned customers on Thursday to patch a critical flaw in its Remote Support (RS) that has been exploited in zero-day attacks since late August. Remote Support is the company's enterprise-grade support solution that helps IT service desks, help desks, and customer support teams troubleshoot issues remotely. Tracked as CVE-2026-102764, this actively exploited authentication bypass vulnerability lets unprivileged remote attackers perform file operations on unpatched appliances and affects RS 26.2.3 or earlier. BeyondTrust patched the security issue for all Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access SaaS customers on October 8, but self-hosted installations must be patched manually if automatic updates are not enabled. "While our internal testing has not identified any way for an attacker to exploit this vulnerability in Privileged Remote Access, PRA shares the affected code, so out of an abundance of caution, we have released the patch for PRA and recommend self-hosted Privileged Remote Access customers apply it immediately," BeyondTrust said.

title: ARMORY CASTLE Exploits BeyondTrust
summary: On October 15, BeyondTrust disclosed a vulnerability, CVE-2026-102764, impacting BeyondTrust Remote Support (formerly Bomgar) appliances. BeyondTrust Remote Support is an enterprise secure remote access solution that enables IT teams to securely access and troubleshoot remote endpoints. The successful exploitation of this vulnerability results in the arbitrary upload of files. During an incident response engagement, Mandiant identified evidence that ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage threat actor (formerly tracked as UNC5221), exploited this vulnerability as a zero-day, in late August 2026. This blog describes how ARMORY CASTLE escalated privileges and established persistent access to compromised BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances following exploitation of CVE-2026-102764, and provides actionable guidance for defenders. Organizations should prepare for potential widespread exploitation following this disclosure, as ARMORY CASTLE and other threat actors have historically conducted broad, opportunistic exploitation once the vulnerability becomes public.

title: Apache CXF: Inoperative max_age authentication-freshness check in OidcClientCodeRequestFilter
summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 9.1, CVEs: CVE-2026-71575, Summary: The max_age authentication-freshness check in OidcClientCodeRequestFilter was inoperative due to a milliseconds/seconds unit mismatch and an inverted comparison polarity. Any relying party using setMaxAgeOffset to enforce re-authentication would silently accept sessions of any age, bypassing step-up authentication policies. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.2.4 or 4.1.9 or 3.6.13, which fix this issue.

title: Authenticated RCE via MCP Stdio transport allows any user to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server
summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Proof-of-Concept, CVSSv3.1: 9.9, CVEs: CVE-2026-105740, Summary: Any authenticated Langflow user can achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the server by adding an MCP server with the "Stdio" transport. The user-supplied command field is passed directly to bash -c "exec {command}" with zero validation, no allowlisting, and no sandboxing. The command executes immediately when the server list is fetched. Additionally, the env field allows arbitrary environment variable injection (e.g., LD_PRELOAD, PATH override). See also: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-105740, See also: https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/langflows-critical-authenticated-rce.html

title: Russia Is Tightening Internet Controls, Leading to Operational Risks
summary: Since mid-2025, the Kremlin has intensified restrictions on digital communications and infrastructure, very likely to suppress the organization of domestic political dissent and conduct digital surveillance within Russia. Increasingly strict measures targeting virtual private networks (VPNs), state-managed internet shutdowns, limitations on civilian communications platforms, and monitoring of domestic and foreign entities very likely represent an escalation from the approaches to censorship and surveillance pursued prior to 2024. However, despite intensifying internet restrictions, technical and political limitations will likely prevent the Kremlin from achieving its long-held objective of a fully “sovereign internet” in the near term. The most likely scenario is that Moscow exerts extensive censorship and monitoring of online activity with increasingly strict –– though not absolute –– controls on circumvention and anonymizing tools. Insikt Group assesses that the Kremlin’s primary objectives regarding internet restrictions are twofold: facilitating extensive surveillance of online activity to support control over the domestic information space while maintaining connectivity to the global internet, and developing national internet infrastructure under Kremlin control, enabling isolation from the global internet if the Kremlin so chooses. Efforts in support of these objectives have almost certainly provided the Kremlin with enhanced ability to control and monitor domestic online discourse.

title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
summary: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet of Things devices and is more resistant to takedown. By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered. Still, the results raise concerns about the possibility of new forms of computer worms.

title: GhostAction Compromises About 1,900 GitHub Accounts, Targets Over 30,000 Repositories
summary: The credential-theft campaign known as GhostAction has ramped up, targeting more than 30,000 repositories across 3,000 users and organizations. The spike, according to GitGuardian, was observed on October 8 and 9, 2026. "This resulted from compromising the GitHub accounts of about 1,900 users. It attempted to extract 3,174 secrets from public repositories' CI," security researchers Gaetan Ferry and Guillaume Valadon said. GhostAction is the moniker for a supply chain attack campaign targeting developer infrastructure on GitHub. Originally discovered in September 2025, it involves threat actors compromising legitimate developer accounts to inject malicious GitHub Actions automation workflows into software repositories. "This payload was deployed in multiple phases," GitGuardian said. "First to 160 previously observed victims, then, 20 minutes later, to 28,000 new repositories between October 8 and 9. New waves have been observed, using the same payload, on October 10 and 12. However, GitHub started preventing the malicious workflow from running starting October 9. Those two subsequent waves therefore could not extract any secrets." Interestingly, a subset of the victims from this new burst were previously compromised in the September 2025 and August 2026 waves, indicating the threat actors are banking on unrotated secrets to pull them off.

title: Help TDS Linked to Hotejka as 20,000+ Cloudflare Pages Domains Host Tech Support Scams
summary: A long-running Traffic Distribution System (TDS) known as Help TDS to a Russian-language affiliate program called Hotejka, which appears to be a rebrand of a traffic monetization operation dubbed ROI777. Help TDS is assessed to be active since at least 2017, offering PHP code templates to partners and affiliates that are installed into compromised websites with an aim to direct unsuspecting users to tech support scams. These scams make use of full-screen browser manipulation and exit prevention techniques to serve bogus Microsoft Windows security alert screens instructing victims to contact a Windows Support number to address the problem. Since April 2026, the scams are run on free Cloudflare Pages sites (*.pages[.]dev), with the threat actor creating roughly 300 disposable pages per day. Over 20,000 such domains have been detected since then. In recent years, Hotejka has also been observed using different aliases on forums like CrackingX, seeking traffic from email spam and access to WordPress admin panels for prices starting at $100. In all, about 20 different affiliates, including Balada Injector, Detour Dog, and DollyWay, send traffic to Help TDS. These operations are known to heavily target WordPress sites to redirect victims to scams and malware.

title: Fake Calendar Invites Target Thousands of Organizations in Microsoft Credential-Phishing Campaign
summary: A calendar invite is one of the most routine messages in the modern workplace. It lands in the inbox, asks for a few seconds of attention, and is rarely questioned. Attackers know this, and they are now using fake meeting invitations to steal Microsoft account credentials. We have identified several large-scale phishing campaigns that abuse fake calendar invites to harvest credentials. Some arrive as an .ics attachment (example 1). The file is valid calendar data, so the attack abuses calendar features and user trust without exploiting a software vulnerability. Others use a link that appears to lead to a different destination (example 2). Both are designed to harvest the victim’s credentials. Check Point Email researchers are tracking these campaigns and have seen a significant surge starting September 25, 2026. A new detection layer specifically designed to identify this type of attack has flagged more than 302,386 unique phishing emails among our customers’ emails, sent to more than 40,000 organizations. The campaigns average more than 8,319 emails per active day. The emails came from more than 33,890 different sender domains and more than 247,270 unique sender addresses.

Check Point Email researchers are tracking these campaigns and have seen a significant surge starting September 25, 2026. A new detection layer specifically designed to identify this type of attack has flagged more than 302,386 unique phishing emails among our

customers’ emails, sent to more than 40,000 organizations. The campaigns average more than 8,319 emails per active day. The emails came from more than 33,890 different sender domains and more than 247,270 unique sender addresses.

title: Ledger asks sellers across Asia to halt sales after supply-chain attack
summary: Ledger is asking resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to halt wallet sales and remove products from shelves while it investigates hardware implant incidents. The company announced the decision in response to discovering that devices purchased from CryptoBilis had been modified to steal seed phrases used to access crypto assets and send them to an unauthorized party over an LTE connection. Ledger sells physical cryptocurrency wallets that securely store private keys used for managing and authorizing digital asset transactions. Following reports of cryptocurrency losses from multiple users, Ledger launched an investigation on October 9 and confirmed that some devices sold by CryptoBilis had been tampered with. Donjon said the implant’s microcontroller detects and decodes the 24-word recovery phrase for setting up and restoring the wallet, then transmits it over LTE using a provisioned eSIM. The implant is a separate component that does not modify the Secure Element or Ledger operating system, or alter transactions or signatures, which makes it undetectable by Ledger’s integrity self-checks.

title: UK Legal Aid Agency: Hackers stole records dating back to 1978
summary: The Legal Aid Agency (LAA), an executive agency of the UK's Ministry of Justice that manages the country's Public Defender Service, says attackers who breached its IT systems in April 2025 stole records dating back to 1978. The agency employs around 1,250 staff, oversees billions in legal funding, and works with approximately 2,000 providers, including barristers, solicitor firms, and non-profit organizations that deliver civil and criminal legal aid services in England and Wales. Two weeks later, it confirmed the resulting data breach was more serious than first believed after finding that attackers had stolen a large trove of sensitive applicant and recipient data from 2010 onward, including contact details, dates of birth, national ID numbers, criminal history, employment status, as well as contribution amounts, debts, and payments. After the LAA breach, which was followed by a string of cyberattacks targeting the Co-op, Harrods, and Marks & Spencer (M&S) UK retail chains ​​​claimed by the DragonForce ransomware operation, the country's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) published guidance and advised UK organizations to follow it to strengthen their cybersecurity defenses.

title: Hackers hijack D-Link, Ubiquiti devices to resell your stolen bandwidth
summary: A proxyjacking campaign has impacted devices in 34 countries, monetizing victims’ internet connections through a commercial residential proxy network. The operator installed Pawns.app, a legitimate bandwidth-sharing application that lets users earn money by sharing their internet connections, on devices without the owners’ consent. Pawns.app account holders are rewarded for allowing traffic from other users to flow through their network, provided it runs on trusted, non-blocking IP addresses. Threat intelligence company GreyNoise discovered the campaign while investigating suspicious activity at an unnamed organization, and identified at least 143 compromised devices worldwide.

title: Fake Arch Linux packages push malware with root privileges
summary: A threat actor uploaded malicious packages to the Arch User Repository (AUR) that impersonated two popular helper tools, yay and paru. AUR is a community-maintained, widely-used package index for Arch Linux and derivative distributions that hosts package build scripts (PKGBUILDs) for third-party and proprietary tools, beta, or older package versions that are no longer available via the official Linux distribution channels. The repository has recently become a target of malicious campaigns, including an attack in June in which 400 packages distributed credential-stealing malware with rootkit capabilities. Another campaign in July prompted Arch to temporarily disable package adoption. The latest campaign was detected on October 13 and involved malicious packages uploaded by a user named “marchos1as” under typosquatted names mimicking the yay and paru command-line tools. Also known as AUR helpers, these tools simplify software management on Arch Linux by streamlining the retrieval and installation of user-contributed packages.

title: NGINX Fixes 5 Flaws, Including Possible RCE and a TLS Bug That May Skip Client-Cert Checks
summary: NGINX released versions 1.30.6 and 1.31.7 on October 14 to fix five vulnerabilities, one of them present in every release since May 2005. There are three memory bugs that F5, the company behind NGINX, says could crash a worker process or possibly let an attacker run code, and each requires a specific configuration to exploit. A fourth lets an attacker forge a TLS session that could get past client-certificate checks, though F5 calls the forgery non-deterministic and beyond the attacker's control. The fifth lets an HTTP/3 client slip extra bytes into a request that NGINX passes on to a backend. None of the five was in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of October 15, and neither NGINX nor F5 reports attacks. NGINX rates all five medium. F5 scores the three memory bugs 9.2, Critical, on CVSS v4.0, the TLS flaw 8.3, and the HTTP/3 flaw 6.9.

title: Drupal Patches Critical Field UI Flaw With Unauthenticated RCE Path via Contributed Modules
summary: Drupal core has a critical flaw in its Field UI module that could let an attacker run code on the site's server, and fixes were shipped on October 14 in Drupal 11.4.10, 11.3.19, and 10.6.19. An attacker cannot reach the flaw through core alone, the Drupal Security Team said in its advisory. Several exploit paths exist through contributed modules, and at least one known path needs no login. Tracked as CVE-2026-108097, the flaw sits in Field UI, the core module behind the admin pages where site builders manage fields and how they display. Drupal rates it 19 out of 25 on its own risk scale, the level the project calls critical.

title: Hackers exploit Collabora RCE flaw to backdoor Nextcloud servers
summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical command execution flaw, now tracked as CVE-2026-110447, in the Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server app (richdocumentscode) for Nextcloud. Multiple administrator reports indicate that attacks began in mid-September, roughly a month before the formal security bulletin, the GitHub advisory, and CVE publication. CVE-2026-110447 impacts richdocumentscode versions before 26.4.303 and resides in the Nextcloud app’s mechanism for starting the bundled Collabora server.

title: Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
summary: Palo Alto Networks has released security updates for a high-severity PAN-OS RCE zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-0322, that has been exploited in attacks targeting firewalls. The vulnerability affects the PAN-OS management interface and lets authenticated attackers with network access execute code as root on vulnerable devices. Palo Alto Networks confirmed in a security advisory published Wednesday that it has seen limited exploitation of the flaw in attacks. "Very limited exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface," the company said. To exploit the vulnerability, attackers need existing credentials and network access to the PAN-OS management interface. Therefore, Palo Alto Networks recommends restricting access to the management interface to trusted internal IP addresses only. The company has released fixes for affected PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2 versions, with a fix for PAN-OS 11.2.16 expected on October 15.

title: Unit 42 Uncovers PEERSTITCH, a Stealthy FortiGate Implant
summary: Unit 42 investigated a multi-stage network intrusion against a telecommunications organization that occurred in September 2024, which we are tracking as cluster CL-STA-0954 (aka UNC5820). The attackers behind CL-STA-0954 achieved an initial compromise by exploiting CVE-2024-47575 against a centralized FortiManager appliance. From that single appliance, our observations are that the attackers exfiltrated an archive containing running configurations, cryptographic material and database files containing information about more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls. Those firewalls protected the target's own infrastructure and the networks of its clients. The discovery of the PEERSTITCH implant demonstrates the increasing technical maturity of edge-device malware. By operating as a one-shot injector, avoiding persistent disk artifacts and building a covert inter-process communication bridge inside process memory, the attackers achieved sustained persistence while evading traditional monitoring. For organizations that manage infrastructure on behalf of others, the management platform is the highest-value target on the network. Compromising the management platform is not contained by the boundary of the organization that owns it. That compromise also does not end when the platform is patched.

title: Asiantuntija järkyttyi – tietävätkö ihmiset, mitä he nyt asentavat laitteelleen?
summary: Metan syyskuun alussa julkaisema tekoälyagentti Muse kohosi nopeasti sovelluslatausten kärkeen Yhdysvalloissa, ja miljoonat ovat ottaneet sen käyttöönsä. Time-lehden mukaan Muse kerää harvinaisen hanakasti käyttäjiensä ja myös muiden ihmisten tietoja. Muse toimii omana sovelluksenaan tai Metan WhatsApp-, Messenger- ja Instagram-sovellusten sisällä. Palvelu ei ole ainakaan toistaiseksi käytössä EU:ssa. Time tarkasteli Musen sisäistä ohjeistusta, joka olisi kaikkien luettavissa. Muse rakentaa käyttäjistään jatkuvasti päivittyviä kansioita keskittyen siihen, ketkä ovat käyttäjälle tärkeitä, mitä käyttäjät himoitsevat ja miten heidän käytöstään voitaisiin hienovaraisesti ohjata. Walsh kuvailee Musea kaupalliseksi vakoiluverkostoksi, joka on naamioitu käyttäjän henkilökohtaiseksi avustajaksi. Asiantuntija painottaa, että Musella on pääsy muun muassa yksityisiin viesteihin, sähköposteihin, pankkitileihin, yhteystietoihin ja henkilökohtaiseen tietoon. Muse ei ole toistaiseksi saatavilla Euroopan unionissa. On epäselvää, miten Metan pitäisi mahdollisesti muuttaa Musea, jotta se noudattaisi EU:n tietosuojalainsäädäntöä. EU:n gdpr-asetus ja digimarkkinasäädös asettavat yrityksille tiukat vaatimukset tietosuojasta ja eri palveluiden tietojen yhdistelemisestä.

title: When a cyberattack breaks the cold chain
summary: For years, people have associated cyberattacks with stolen data, locked computers and disrupted digital services. However, the incident that affected numerous French supermarkets during the night of 11–12 October 2026 shows that a breach can have consequences beyond the digital world. This time, the attackers did not primarily target tills, payment systems or customer databases. Their target was the connected infrastructure used to regulate food refrigeration across different stores. This incident is particularly significant because it clearly shows how a digital vulnerability can directly affect products, facilities and physical processes. Hospitals, factories, energy providers, transport companies, logistics centres and water treatment facilities all rely on connected systems to manage physical processes. In each of these environments, an insecure configuration, poorly protected remote access or an outdated device can become an entry point. Causing a significant impact on critical or sensitive infrastructure does not always require an extremely sophisticated attack. A controller exposed to the Internet, weak credentials, insufficiently protected remote access or poor segmentation between IT and OT networks can open the door to serious operational consequences.

title: Unmasking EvilTokens: Getting to the root of device code phishing
summary: Following its emergence in February 2026, EvilTokens quickly became one of the most widely used phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platforms, providing cybercriminals with AI capabilities for tailoring phishing lures and analyzing compromised inboxes to identify high-value targets. This AI-powered cybercrime platform facilitated sophisticated business email compromise (BEC) campaigns that compromised more than 12,000 inboxes in over 10,000 organizations worldwide. EvilTokens enabled threat actors to abuse the device code authentication flow, steal tokens, and compromise organizational accounts at scale using an AI-driven infrastructure and automating multiple parts of the attack chain. The toolkit offered a plethora of prebuilt phishing templates and landing pages with an AI-powered assistant to aid in structuring target-specific emails. To harden networks against the device code phishing activity described above, defenders can implement the following: - Only allow device code flow where necessary. Microsoft recommends blocking device code flow wherever possible. Where necessary, configure Microsoft Entra ID’s device code flow in your Conditional Access policies.

title: When LLM Gateways Go Wrong: Findings from LiteLLM
summary: This security assessment of LiteLLM revealed multiple high-risk vulnerabilities that could be chained together to achieve remote code execution, arbitrary file access, and complete system compromise. The most severe issue, the missing authorization checks in /config/update combined with environment variable injection, demonstrates how a single oversight in access control can cascade into multiple high-impact exploitation paths. LiteLLM represents an important innovation in the LLM ecosystem, providing a unified interface and management layer for interacting with language models. The rapid development pace in this space has produced powerful tools that solve real problems for organizations deploying AI systems at scale. However, speed of innovation must not come at the expense of fundamental security practices. The vulnerabilities documented here are not novel attack classes; they include missing authorization checks, path traversal, RCE via dynamic module loading, and insecure password storage. These are well-understood security issues with established mitigation patterns. Their presence in production code highlights a concerning trend: as the AI and LLM ecosystem races forward, traditional security fundamentals are sometimes treated as secondary concerns.

title: Cyber incident hits grocery stores in US, Netherlands and Belgium
summary: Ahold Delhaize, the Dutch multinational retailer, announced Monday it was taking precautionary measures following a cybersecurity incident, with stores in the U.S., Netherlands and Belgium reportedly impacted. Distribution centers, online grocery orders and in-store pricing have been disrupted, although it is unclear whether this was due to the incident itself or the precautionary measures. The company said its teams “are taking steps to assess and mitigate the issue,” including “taking some systems offline to help protect them.” Albert Heijn's website, app and customer service were unavailable, grocery deliveries were suspended, and electronic shelf labels displayed outdated promotional prices. The brand said it had disconnected systems to protect its IT environment but gave no timeline for restoring services.

title: U.S. Shuts Down Over 40 Laptop Farms, Charges 14 in North Korean IT Worker Fraud
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) on Tuesday charged 14 people and seized about 187 computers as part of its ongoing efforts to disrupt North Korea's fraudulent remote IT worker (ITW) scheme. The indictment charges a mix of U.S. citizens and Chinese nationals for their roles in an IT worker conspiracy affecting more than 70 U.S. companies, charging them with wire fraud conspiracy, money laundering conspiracy, conspiracy to commit identity theft, and aggravated identity theft. Cybersecurity company CrowdStrike, which investigated indicators associated with suspected fake IT workers and identified links between apparently unrelated employees and laptop-hosting locations, said the threat actors have resorted to a variety of techniques to direct employer-provided hardware to laptop farm addresses during the onboarding phase. The FBI said it also identified cases where the threat actors have used threats of physical violence against former managers and their families to demand payments and coerce others to carry out actions that further the scheme, marking a newfound escalation of the threat. Besides using stolen identities to apply for jobs, the IT workers are known to falsely claim ownership of social media accounts, professional profiles, and online identities belonging to other individuals in the tech sector to lend a veneer of legitimacy to their applications.

Besides using stolen identities to apply for jobs, the IT workers are known to falsely claim ownership of social media accounts, professional profiles, and online identities belonging to other individuals in the tech sector to lend a veneer of legitimacy to their applications.

title: AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host
summary: A flaw in Linux's vhost subsystem lets a local user read and write kernel memory at will and become root across nearly a decade of kernel versions. In one virtualization setup, it lets an untrusted virtual machine write to the host's memory and hijack the program that runs the virtual machine. The bug is tracked as CVE-2026-74580 and named Vghost. Tencent Zhuque Lab, which found the flaw, released a fix on August 3 and published a full write-up on October 12 with working demos of both attacks. There is no public sign it has been exploited yet. vhost keeps a small cache of the memory mappings behind each virtual ring and the shared queues it uses to move data. A cache hit is treated as proof that the region was already checked. The cache is cleared when the mapping is updated or invalidated and when the queue is reset, but not when the VHOST_SET_VRING_ADDR or VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM commands change the ring's addresses or size while the queue is live. The flaw affects Linux kernels from 4.11 up to 7.2-rc4. Tencent reproduced the full local-user-to-root chain on five distribution kernels: Ubuntu 26.04, RHEL 9.8, Amazon Linux 2023, Microsoft Azure Linux 3.0, and Oracle Linux 10.2. On Ubuntu, the device node was limited to the kvm group, so the starting point there was a member of that group rather than any user.

title: Heart Monitor Firm Notifying at Least 370,000 Patients of Hack
summary: The San Francisco, California-based company in recent days submitted breach reports to several state attorneys general, including Texas and South Carolina. iRhythm reported nearly 300,000 Texans and nearly 70,000 South Carolinians affected in those two states alone. But in recent days, a handful of media outlets, including BeInsure, reported that the iRhythm incident affected a total of nearly 8.2 million people. iRhythm in a June 10 filing to the SEC said it received demands from a threat actor for an undisclosed payment in exchange for not publicly releasing the stolen data, including proprietary data, patient protected health information and other personal information. Other hacks include an Iranian hacktivist attack on medical equipment maker Stryker in February that affected manufacturing and distribution processes for several weeks; a cyber incident at device maker Medtronic in April that affected corporate IT systems; and an August cyberattack on Boston Scientific that triggered a global network outage, shutting down manufacturing plants and distribution centers.

title: Global takedown hits network behind 1 billion phishing messages
summary: A massive cybercriminal ecosystem facilitating more than a billion malicious messages targeting over 75,000 organizations across 150 countries has been disrupted by law enforcement agencies and partners worldwide. Since the start of the year, more than 750 million malicious messages have been aimed at Microsoft customers via email and SMS texts. Following an investigation initiated by Microsoft and Japan’s National Police Agency (NPA) into a wave of fraudulent activity, "a sprawling Chinese-language cybercrime marketplace" was discovered, with tools and services for phishing campaigns. Under an order from the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida, Microsoft and Health-ISAC seized and redirected domains supporting YAM Store, CoGUI, and Iron Man. The tech giant also deactivated over 20,000 accounts associated with the YAM Store and blocked 100,000 domains the cybercriminals used for impersonation and fraud. Currently, more infrastructure is being removed based on the findings of the investigation, which also involves the Japanese authorities, JC3, Resecurity, Cloudflare, Oracle, Proofpoint, and TRM Labs.

title: curl Patches HTTP/2 Upload Flaw After PoC Demonstrates Client-Side Code Execution
summary: A flaw in how curl handles HTTP/2 uploads lets a malicious server receiving an upload corrupt the client's memory, and the researcher who reported it turned that into code execution on the uploading machine. The curl project fixed it on October 14 in curl 8.23.0. Taking over a client needs exact knowledge of its build and memory layout, and curl expects a real attack to end in a crash instead. The flaw, a use-after-free tracked as CVE-2026-92392, affects curl and libcurl 8.12.0 through 8.22.0, both the command-line tool and the library that many other programs use for transfers. curl rates it High on its own four-level scale, its first High-severity flaw since the SOCKS5 heap overflow of October 2023. The project cut its release cycle by two weeks to ship the fix.

title: Cisco patches new Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks
summary: Cisco has patched another actively exploited zero-day flaw in its Secure Email Gateway (SEG) that lets remote unauthenticated attackers execute commands with root privileges. Tracked as CVE-2026-76519, this vulnerability stems from a relative path traversal weakness in SEG's Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature, caused by improper handling of email attachments. Threat actors can exploit this issue by sending an email with a maliciously crafted attachment through an unpatched device. "A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system," Cisco said in a Wednesday advisory. "In October 2026, the Cisco PSIRT became aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability."

title: CISA warns admins to immediately fix Ivanti flaw exploited as zero-day
summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) urged security teams to immediately patch an Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) flaw exploited in zero-day attacks since at least October 1st. Tracked as CVE-2026-104935, this high-severity authentication bypass vulnerability lets remote threat actors without privileges execute arbitrary commands on targeted ICS systems in low-complexity attacks that don't require user interaction. Ivanti released ICS versions 22.8R2.5, 25.1.3.0, 25.1.3.1, and 25.1.1.2 on Tuesday to address this security flaw and warned customers to "act immediately" because of "limited exploitation in the wild."

title: Ransomware gets personal: 'We-know-where-you-are kind of stuff'
summary: Tim Beasley, a senior incident response consultant at Semperis, was investigating a cyberattack involving Russia’s Midnight Blizzard when a package containing nesting dolls and other regional gifts showed up on his doorstep. At the time, Beasley served as the lead investigator for Microsoft’s Detection and Response Team (DART). He assumed it was from the group, which has been linked to the Kremlin’s Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR), although the sender didn’t leave a note. “Just little souvenirs and gift basket stuff from that area of the world,” he told The Register. “We-know-where-you-are kind of stuff. It’s a real eye-opener when you get that type of thing.” This type of psychological intimidation and harm against victim companies’ employees has seen an uptick in the last several years to the point where it's almost common. Thirty-seven percent of ransomware attacks involved psychological or physical threats against staff, according to Semperis’ annual ransomware risk report. The global study of 1,200 post-ransomware organizations conducted over the first half of the year found attackers threatening psychological intimidation (23 percent) and physical threats (17 percent), to force payment. They are not only targeting executives and staff, but also families of their victims. The takeaway for defenders and executives from this report is to “stand your ground,” Beasley said. “Don’t buckle under the pressure, and just know that you know it's going to be okay. If you feel like you're under duress, then by all means get law enforcement involved. Don't be afraid to call the cops. Don't be afraid to get the FBI involved, sooner rather than later. And don’t pay them.”

title: Break the silence: Kazakhstan-nexus UAT-6275 targets CIS government organizations
summary: Cisco Talos identified UAT-6275 (TAG-193 by Recorded Future) activity targeting government organizations across the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS). Recovered artifacts show additional interest in water resources and energy. This focus is consistent with intelligence collection and may reflect the regional effects of the Russia–Ukraine war. - In activity observed from June 2025 through August 2026, Talos identified four infection-chain types that use macro-enabled documents, PS2EXE downloaders, GitHub-hosted PowerShell, and a crafted WinRAR archive exploiting CVE-2025-8088. The recovered payloads include several custom reverse shells that provide interactive remote access. - Three publicly accessible staging directories and GitHub repository history exposed payload builds, tool inventories, and changes to command-and-control (C2) infrastructure. These operational security lapses gave us direct visibility into the group's recent activity. - The files recovered from the exposed infrastructure suggest preparation for post-compromise operations and potential activity against Linux hosts and internet-facing appliances.

Ruandan, Burundin, Tansanian, Keski-Afrikan tasavallan ja Etelä-Sudanin rajaseuduilla liikkuminen on vaarallista kapinallis- ja rikollisjoukkioiden tekemien väkivaltaisten ryöstöjen takia. Onnettomuuden myötä Kafue-jokeen virtaava Mwambashi-joki ja sitä ympäröivät maa-alueet saastuivat terveydelle vakavasti vaarallisista päästöistä, ml. raskasmetalleista.
